prompt: The number of goals $X$ a soccer team scores in a match has distribution $P(0) = 0.3$, $P(1) = 0.4$, $P(2) = 0.3$. Find the variance $\sigma_X^2$. Round to the nearest tenth.
hint: First find the mean. Then variance is $\sum (x - \mu)^2 \cdot P(x)$.

hints.text: First find the mean. Then variance is $\sum (x - \mu)^2 \cdot P(x)$.
The mean is $0(0.3) + 1(0.4) + 2(0.3) = 1$. Now square each distance from $1$ and weight by probability.

explanation: Variance weights each squared distance from the mean by its probability: $(0-1)^2(0.3) = 0.3$, $(1-1)^2(0.4) = 0$, $(2-1)^2(0.3) = 0.3$.
Sum: $\sigma_X^2 = 0.6$. (The standard deviation would be $\sqrt{0.6} \approx 0.77$ goals.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Use symmetry
steps: The distribution is symmetric around $1$ (0.3 on each side), so the mean is exactly $1$ with no arithmetic.
Only $X = 0$ and $X = 2$ are away from the mean, each 1 unit away, each with probability $0.3$.
